alt: 3248 Paper 2 lasts 1 hour 30 minutes for 50 marks, 50% of the qualification, with four compulsory exercises: sentence transformation (5 marks), multiple-choice cloze (10), extended writing of about 200 words (20) and translation of about 150 words from English into Urdu (15). Only Exercise 4 has its question in English.
caption: Four compulsory exercises; writing and translation carry most of the marks.

after: ## Where this fits in Cambridge O-Level Urdu
alt: 3247 First Language Urdu's Paper 2 tests literary set texts; 3248 Second Language Urdu's Paper 2 tests applied language: grammar in context, extended writing and translation from English into Urdu.
caption: This paper exists only in 3248: it tests applied language, not literature.

alt: Each of five sentences is rewritten according to a prompt, such as a change of tense, voice or sentence type, while keeping exactly the same meaning. With one mark per sentence, verb endings, postpositions, word order and unchanged meaning all need checking.
caption: Five marks, five sentences: precise grammar, identical meaning.

alt: The ten grammar points the syllabus names for the cloze: verb conjugation, subject/verb agreement, comparatives, superlatives, parts of speech, nouns, prepositions, postpositions, articles and context vocabulary. Each option must fit grammatically and make sense in the passage.
caption: An option can be grammatical in isolation and still wrong for the passage.

alt: Exercise 3 is worth 20 marks: about 200 words of continuous prose from short prompts, with purpose, format and audience specified, for example a letter, a diary entry or a description. Prepare for narrative, descriptive, persuasive and informational purposes.
caption: The biggest single exercise: practise every purpose, not just one.

alt: An English passage of about 150 words is translated into Urdu for 15 marks. A word-for-word translation that gives unnatural Urdu is marked down; an accurate translation that reads naturally scores better.
caption: Keep the meaning exactly, but make the Urdu sound like Urdu.

alt: Marks by exercise: 5 for sentence transformation, 10 for the cloze, 20 for extended writing and 15 for translation, so Exercises 3 and 4 carry 35 of the 50 marks. Secure the named grammar points, then prioritise timed writing and translation practice.
caption: Writing and translation carry 35 of 50 marks: weight revision accordingly.
